sentences: Direct-sum questions study how learning resources change when several tasks are combined into a product class.
This source asks how learning curves, uniform-convergence rates, and related complexity parameters scale relative to their single-task versions.
For some realizable settings, learning components separately gives a simple additive error bound, but it is unclear when joint learning can improve it.
Excess-risk and uniform-convergence quantities need separate analysis because their differences do not inherit the same elementary bound.
Sharp product rules would explain when solving several learning problems together provides a statistical advantage over treating them independently.
